doc.title: Phil Schaap interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003

title: Freedom on the air and meeting Walter Page
summary: He has complete liberty on his show; recalls meeting Walter Page and Jack Washington as a child.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: You’ve got a show — were you pretty much at liberty to play what you wanted?
Complete liberty. That’s why I’m still there.
Because if someone was telling you—

Then there’d be no point to it. I mean if like somebody’s going to tell me what Basie record to play, that’s kind of silly. I mean if Jo Jones told me to play it, that’s fine. But I mean that’s weird. I mean Herschel Evans died before I was born. Everybody else I met, most of them were close friends. I mean I even met Walter Page at six, and I think I met Jack Washington when he was in town when I was seven. It was real hello-goodbye quick with Jo Jones, but I was there. I remember the one with Page, on the street, I have no idea what street, “This man is Mr. Page, we call him ‘Biggum,’ you say ‘hello Mr. Page.’” I said, “Hello Mr. Page.” And he shook my hand and that was it. But that I remember.
